pages.text: Guizhouichthyosaurus tangae comes from the Triassic, with fossils found in the Xiaowa and Zhuganpo Formations, South China. It is a large ichthyosaur, growing up to 7 m in length, with undescribed specimens reportedly attaining larger sizes. Its snout is notably long and powerful, being able to consume large marine reptiles, with one fossil specimen containing the remains of a thalattosaur in the stomach region, solidifying it as an apex predator.

Guizhouicthyosaurus is also notable in that it shows that icthyosaurs not only managed to attain large sizes very early on, but were also incredibly efficient swimmers, even in the early stages of their evolution, despite Guizhouicthyosaurus using a less-efficient eel-like motion.
